extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (ordinary users and library authors), especially those needing library procedure reference for modular, parallel, poly, random, resources, and ring operations
extracted.subtask_description: API-style reference entries for SINGULAR libraries (modular, parallel, poly, random, resources, ring), documenting usage, returns, notes, and examples for each procedure. Useful for developers writing code/scripts using these libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: modular
rubrics_metrics.description: modular(command, arguments[, primeTest, deleteUnluckyPrimes, pTest, finalTest, pmax]) — apply command to arguments using modular methods; optional test procedures control prime filtering and final verification; pmax bounds primes used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: result of command applied to arguments, computed via modular methods. Result type must be bigint, ideal, module, or matrix. Optional arguments default to 'all tests succeed' and primes assumed lucky. pmax default is 2147483647 (or 536870909 for certain baserings). See Section D.4.13.1 [modStd] for algorithm details. Example shown computing std on an ideal; see notes about role of primeTest/deleteUnluckyPrimes/pTest/finalTest.

rubrics_metrics.name: parallel (library overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: parallel.lib — abstraction layer providing implementations of several parallel skeletons built on tasks.lib; intended for ordinary users and library authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: provide parallel 'skeletons' for task interaction. References: tasks.lib, modnormal.lib, modstd.lib, resources.lib. Author: Andreas Steenpass. Examples and cross-references given throughout the parallel.* entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: parallelWaitN
rubrics_metrics.description: parallelWaitN(commands, arguments, N[, timeout]) — waits for N jobs to finish and returns a list of results of commands[i] applied to arguments[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list containing results (type depends on tasks); entries for tasks that didn't finish due to timeout/error are 'none'. Returned list may contain more than N results if several jobs finish simultaneously and may contain fewer in case of timeout/errors. commands entries must be strings; arguments entries must be lists. Optional timeout in ms (default 0 disables). Example shows running two 'std' commands and waiting for 1 result.

rubrics_metrics.name: parallelWaitFirst
rubrics_metrics.description: parallelWaitFirst(commands, arguments[, timeout]) — synonym for parallelWaitN(..., N=1); returns at least one result (if no timeout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same usage rules and behavior as parallelWaitN with N=1. Example provided; cross-references to parallelWaitN and parallelWaitAll.

rubrics_metrics.name: parallelWaitAll
rubrics_metrics.description: parallelWaitAll(commands, arguments[, timeout]) — wait for all jobs (size(arguments)) to finish and return list of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synonymous to parallelWaitN(commands, arguments, size(arguments)[, timeout]). As a shortcut, commands can be a string, which duplicates it for each argument entry. Optional timeout in ms (default 0 disables). Example shows three tasks returning three result blocks. See parallelWaitN/parallelWaitFirst for related behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: parallelTestAND
rubrics_metrics.description: parallelTestAND(commands, arguments[, timeout]) — tests whether commands[i] applied to arguments[i] evaluate to non-zero for all i; returns 1 if all non-zero, 0 otherwise (or -1 on timeout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries of commands must be strings; arguments entries must be lists. Each commands[i] applied to arguments[i] must evaluate to an integer. Shortcut: commands may be string duplicated for all arguments. Optional timeout in ms (default 0). Example tests 'size' across arguments and returns 1 or 0. See parallelTestOR.

rubrics_metrics.name: parallelTestOR
rubrics_metrics.description: parallelTestOR(commands, arguments[, timeout]) — returns 1 if any commands[i] applied to arguments[i] is non-zero, 0 otherwise (or -1 on timeout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same constraints as parallelTestAND. Shortcut: commands can be a string. Optional timeout in ms (default 0). Example provided testing 'size' across a list of different argument types.

rubrics_metrics.name: poly.lib (library purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: poly.lib — procedures for manipulating polynomials, ideals, modules: provides many utilities for common algebraic operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors listed. Cross-references to other library sections. The following procedures (cyclic, elemSymmId, katsura, freerank, is_zero, lcm, maxcoef, maxdeg, maxdeg1, mindeg, mindeg1, normalize, rad_con, content, mod2id, id2mod, substitute, subrInterred, newtonDiag, hilbPoly) are defined with usages, returns, notes and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: cyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: cyclic(n) — returns the ideal of cyclic n-roots from the first n variables of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: cyclic(nvars(basering)) prints the cyclic ideal generators; homog(cyclic(5),z) example shows homogenization. Return: ideal. Usage: input n integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: elemSymmId
rubrics_metrics.description: elemSymmId — returns the ideal of elementary symmetric polynomials for the first n variables of the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage with explicit n or nvars(basering) shown. Examples show output of elementary symmetric polynomials. Return: ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: katsura
rubrics_metrics.description: katsura([n]) — returns the n-th Katsura ideal, either creating a new ring if necessary or using the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior depends on nvars(basering) relative to n. Examples show generated ideals and how basering may be changed. Return: katsura ideal. Notes on naming/ordering appear in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: freerank
rubrics_metrics.description: freerank(M[,any]) — compute rank of module presented by M if it is free; returns rank or -1 if not free. With second argument returns list [rank, minbase(M)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: vdim(coker(M)/m*coker(M)) if coker(M) is free; 0-module free of rank 0. freerank(syz(M)) computes rank of M if free. Examples demonstrate cases returning 2, -1, etc., and use of second argument to return minimal base.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_zero
rubrics_metrics.description: is_zero(M[,any]) — tests whether coker(M) = 0 treating M as a matrix; returns integer 1 if zero, 0 otherwise. With second argument returns [L1 (1/0), L2 = dim(M)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M can be poly/ideal/vector/module/matrix. Examples show usage on modules and ideals; case returning 1 for ideal equal to zero modulo quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: lcm
rubrics_metrics.description: lcm(p[,q]) — computes least common multiple: for integer inputs returns int lcm; for polynomial/ideal returns polynomial lcm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Usage supports int/intvec and poly/ideal with list q. Examples show lcm of polynomials and integers, including lcm of ideals by passing ideal and poly. Return type depends on input type.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxcoef
rubrics_metrics.description: maxcoef(f) — returns maximal length (number of characters) of coefficients of polynomial/vector/module/matrix f as integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate lengths for large integer coefficients and rationals; returns 10/11 in examples. Useful for measuring coefficient size. Return: int.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxdeg
rubrics_metrics.description: maxdeg(id) — returns maximal degree(s) of monomials in id independent of ring ordering; returns int for poly, intmat for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows usage with weighted orderings. Note: maxdeg1 returns a single integer (or vector) in some cases and can be faster for single polynomials. See maxdeg1 for alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxdeg1
rubrics_metrics.description: maxdeg1(id[,v]) — returns the maximal [weighted] degree of monomials of id independent of ring ordering; default variable weights v = 1..1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns an integer (or respects provided intvec v). For one polynomial with no intvec, maxdeg1 is faster than maxdeg. Examples illustrate weighted degrees and use of ringweights.

rubrics_metrics.name: mindeg
rubrics_metrics.description: mindeg(id) — returns minimal degree(s) of monomials of id independent of ring ordering; int if poly else intmat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage with ord and uses for matrices. Returns minimal degrees; see mindeg1 for weighted variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: mindeg1
rubrics_metrics.description: mindeg1(id[,v]) — returns minimal [weighted] degree of monomials of id independent of ring ordering; mindeg1 of i-th variable is v[i] (default v=1..1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns integer. For single polynomials without v, mindeg1 is faster. Examples show negative values when weights allow negative degrees and matrix use cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalize
rubrics_metrics.description: normalize(id) — normalize polynomial/vector/ideal/module: each element normalized with leading coefficient equal to 1; returns object of same type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show normalization of polynomials and modules (leading coefficients scaled to 1). Behavior with coefficient ring blocks (c,ls) shown. Return: normalized object.

rubrics_metrics.name: rad_con
rubrics_metrics.description: rad_con(g, I) — tests containment of polynomial g in the radical of ideal I; returns 1 if contained, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return type int. Examples show rad_con returning 0 or 1 depending on membership in radical; works over specified basering.

rubrics_metrics.name: content
rubrics_metrics.description: content(f) — returns content (gcd of coefficients) of polynomial or vector f as a number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates returning 3 for polynomial with integer coefficients; vector content returns gcd across entries. Cross-reference: cleardenom in Section 5.1.9.

rubrics_metrics.name: mod2id
rubrics_metrics.description: mod2id(M, vpos) — convert module M to an ideal by replacing gen(i) with new ring variables var(vpos[i]) and adding monomials var(vpos[i])*var(vpos[j]) to generators so e(i)*e(j)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes basering contains variables var(vpos[i]) that don't occur in M. Returns ideal suitable for rings where module components correspond to new variables; intended when passing to ring with new variables e(1)..e(s) s.t. e(i)*e(j)=0. Example shows resulting ideal; note about vpos mapping.

rubrics_metrics.name: id2mod
rubrics_metrics.description: id2mod(I, vpos) — inverse of mod2id: replace var(vpos[i]) by gen(i) and omit monomial generators var(vpos[i])*var(vpos[j]) returning module corresponding to ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only valid if ideal contains all var(vpos[i])*var(vpos[j]) as monomial generators and other generators are linear combinations of var(vpos[i]) over other variables. Should be applied only to ideals created by mod2id with same vpos. Example demonstrates conversion back to module.

rubrics_metrics.name: substitute
rubrics_metrics.description: substitute(I, v, f[, v1, f1, ...]) — substitute ring variables by polynomials/ideals: two cases: (1) polynomials substitution for variables; (2) ideal substitution where v is ideal and f ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends built-in subst via maps. Case 1: replaces variables v, v1,... by polynomials f,f1,... in order. Case 2: v[i] substituted by f[i] up to min(size(v), ncols(f)). Examples show substitution usage and results; useful for maps and variable transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: subrInterred
rubrics_metrics.description: subrInterred(mon, sm, iv) — interreduce only with respect to a subset of variables: given mon (monomial generators not divisible by t_i), sm an ideal in ring with x's and t's, and iv listing variables to be used as x_i, returns interreduced generators as a k[t]-submodule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list l with l[1] monomials in order, l[2] their coefficients after interreduction, l[3] product l[1]*l[2]. Purpose: perform interreduction only wrt subset of variables. Examples show outputs for different ideals and variable selections.

rubrics_metrics.name: newtonDiag
rubrics_metrics.description: newtonDiag(f) — compute Newton diagram of polynomial f; returns intmat where each row is exponent vector of a monomial of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute Newton diagram. Example shows output rows for monomials of f = x^2 y + 3 x z - 5 y + 3. Return: int matrix of exponents.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbPoly
rubrics_metrics.description: hilbPoly(I) — compute Hilbert polynomial of basering/I where I is homogeneous; returns intvec v = v0,...,vr such that Hilbert polynomial is (v0 + v1*t + ... + vr * t^r)/r!.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: intvec encoding Hilbert polynomial coefficients. Example shows call with a long homogeneous ideal and output intvec [-11,10].

rubrics_metrics.name: random.lib (library purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: random.lib — procedures to create random and sparse matrices, ideals, polynomials for testing and experimentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides utilities (genericid, randomid, randommat, sparseid, sparsematrix, sparsemat, sparsepoly, sparsetriag, sparseHomogIdeal, triagmatrix, randomLast, randomBinomial) with parameters controlling sparsity, bounds, degrees, and randomness. Notes recommend small bounds b in characteristic 0 for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: genericid
rubrics_metrics.description: genericid(id[,p,b]) — returns system of generators of id which are generic, sparse, tridiagonal linear combinations of given generators; coefficients in [1,b] and sparsity p percent (default p=75,b=30000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: new system of generators. Note: for performance try smaller b in characteristic 0. Examples show generated combinations for ideals and modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: randomid
rubrics_metrics.description: randomid(id[,k,b]) — returns ideal/module having k generators which are random linear combinations of generators of id with coefficients in [-b,b] (defaults b=30000, k=size(id)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use smaller b in char 0 for performance. Examples show random combinations and modules; show how to print module generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: randommat
rubrics_metrics.description: randommat(n, m[, id, b]) — returns n x m matrix with entries random linear combinations of elements of id and coefficients in [-b,b] (defaults id=maxideal(1), b=30000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: matrix. Note: for performance, use small b in characteristic 0. Examples show random matrices of polynomials and linear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: sparseid
rubrics_metrics.description: sparseid(k, u[, o, p, b]) — build ideal with k generators, each of degree d with u <= d <= o, p percent of terms in degree d are zero, remaining have random coefficients in [1,b] (defaults o=u, p=75, b=30000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: ideal. Examples demonstrate typical generated sparse polynomials with specified sparsity and coefficient bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: sparsematrix
rubrics_metrics.description: sparsematrix(n, m, o[, u, pe, pp, b]) — returns n x m matrix with about pe percent zero entries; non-zero entries random polynomials of degree d, u<=d<=o, with pp percent of terms zero; coefficients in [1,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults (pe,u,pp,b) = (0,50,75,100). Examples show matrices of sparse polys and dense matrices of sparse linear forms. Use parameters to control sparsity and degree.

rubrics_metrics.name: sparsemat
rubrics_metrics.description: sparsemat(n, m[, p, b]) — returns n x m integer matrix with p percent zeros and remaining random integers between 1 and b (defaults p=75,b=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: integer matrix. Examples show varying sparsity and random values.

rubrics_metrics.name: sparsepoly
rubrics_metrics.description: sparsepoly(u[, o, p, b]) — returns a polynomial having only terms in degree d with u<=d<=o, p percent of the terms zero and remaining with random coefficients in [1,b] (defaults: o=u, p=75, b=30000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: polynomial. Examples show generated sparse polynomials for test cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: sparsetriag
rubrics_metrics.description: sparsetriag(n, m[, p, b]) — returns n x m lower triangular integer matrix with diagonal entries 1, about p percent of lower diagonal entries zero, remaining random integers in [1,b] (defaults p=75,b=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: integer lower triangular matrix. Examples show behavior for different sparsity settings; diagonal remains ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: sparseHomogIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: sparseHomogIdeal(k, u[, o, p, b]) — returns ideal with k homogeneous generators, each random degree in [u,o], p percent of terms zero, remaining coefficients in [1,b] (defaults o=u,p=75,b=30000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: homogeneous ideal. Examples show returned homogeneous polynomials with controlled sparsity and degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: triagmatrix
rubrics_metrics.description: triagmatrix(n, m, o[, u, pe, pp, b]) — returns n x m lower triangular matrix with diagonal entries 1 and non-zero lower entries random polynomials of degree d (u<=d<=o) with sparsity controls pe, pp and coefficient bound b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults (pe,u,pp,b) = (0,50,75,100). Examples show sparse triagonal matrices of polynomials and dense triagonal of sparse linear forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: randomLast
rubrics_metrics.description: randomLast(b) — returns maximal ideal where the last variable is replaced by a random linear combination of all variables with coefficients in [-b,b], except last variable has coefficient 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: ideal. Example shows ideal with last generator replaced by -x+z given b=10.

rubrics_metrics.name: randomBinomial
rubrics_metrics.description: randomBinomial(k, u[, o, b]) — returns a binomial ideal with k homogeneous generators of degree d with u<=d<=o and randomly chosen monomials and coefficients in [-b,b] (defaults u=o,b=10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: binomial ideal. Example shows generators like -x^4 z - x z^4 etc. Useful for testing binomial ideal algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: resources.lib (library purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: resources.lib — tools to manage computational resources of a SINGULAR session; tasks.lib and dependent libraries respect these settings and will not use more resources than provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedures to set/get cores and semaphores; implementations are simple and can be extended to distributed computations. Cross-references to parallel and tasks libraries.

rubrics_metrics.name: addcores
rubrics_metrics.description: addcores(n) — adjust the number of available processor cores by adding n (can be negative); result must be >= 1 and may take time to reduce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be called in main process only and not within tasks defined via tasks.lib. Returns the adjusted number. Examples show setcores then addcores(-2). See setcores/getcores.

rubrics_metrics.name: setcores
rubrics_metrics.description: setcores(n) — set number of available processor cores to n (n >= 1); returns n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be called in main process only and not inside tasks. Reducing cores may take time. Examples demonstrate setcores(2) and setcores(4). See addcores/getcores.

rubrics_metrics.name: getcores
rubrics_metrics.description: getcores() — return the number of available processor cores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be called in main process only. Example: setcores(4); getcores() -> 4. See setcores/addcores.

rubrics_metrics.name: semaphore
rubrics_metrics.description: semaphore(n) — create a new semaphore initialized with value n and return its index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates acquiring, try_acquire, release and try_acquire behavior with the returned semaphore index and system('semaphore', ...) calls. Useful for resource synchronization across tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: ring.lib (library purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: ring.lib — procedures for manipulating rings and maps: change characteristics, change monomial ordering, and rename variables among other ring manipulation utilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors: Singular team. Cross-references to other ring/Qring procedures and examples. The following procedures are included: changechar, changeord, changevar (documented here).

rubrics_metrics.name: changechar
rubrics_metrics.description: changechar(c[, r]) — return ring R obtained from ring r (default basering) by changing ringlist(r)[1] to c (i.e., change characteristic/coefficient ring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: ring object. Examples show changing to ZZ/2(A), then to ZZ/32003. Use setring to switch to returned ring and kill rings afterward to cleanup. Works with coefficient blocks and variable blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: changeord
rubrics_metrics.description: changeord(neword[, r]) — change monomial ordering of ring r (default basering) to neword; returns new ring R with updated ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: neword is specified as list forms (e.g., list(list('wp', intvec(2,3)), list(list('dp', 1:(n-2))))). Example shows changeord to a block weighted ordering and using changeord on a qring returned by std(i) then setting ring. Use when you need a ring with a different ordering for computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: changevar
rubrics_metrics.description: changevar(vars[, r]) — change variable names/strings of ring r (default basering) according to vars (string); supports renaming to t(1)..t(n) or explicit comma-separated names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for avoiding variable name conflicts (e.g., when using ringtensor). This procedure uses 'execute' internally to effect rename. Example context shown but specific examples truncated in chunk.
